## Graphmem 0.14.0

This release makes it easier to keep memory tidy. Two new plugin skills save a session's durable facts and merge overlapping memories into fewer dense ones, the MCP server gains a `list` tool for browsing memories, and `inspect` and `gmem show` now return a memory's entities and the relations between them. A new `gmem tokens` command shows which memories exceed the embedding model's limit. The `gmem` binary and the Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi plugin packages are versioned 0.14.0.

### What's new

- **Memory sync and compact skills.** The plugin ships `graphmem-memory-sync` (save a session's durable facts) and `graphmem-memory-compact` (merge memories into fewer dense ones). Both run only on request, and memory content is written in English by default.
- **MCP `list` tool.** Pages through memories newest first, unranked, with their entities and full content, in the same scopes `recall` reads. It does not change access counts. `gmem list` gains `--offset`.
- **`gmem tokens`.** Counts tokens with the active embedding model's tokenizer from the local model cache, for a piece of text, one memory (`--id`), or every memory over the model's limit (`--over-limit`).
- **Entities and relations in `inspect` and `gmem show`.** Both now return the memory's entities and the relations between them.

### Upgrading

For npm installs, upgrade the package and refresh the binary with `gmem-install`:

```sh
npm install --global @sonic182/graphmem@0.14.0
gmem-install
gmem version
```

MCP clients can also run the package directly with `npx -y @sonic182/graphmem@0.14.0 mcp`. For manual installs, download the archive for your platform below and replace the existing `gmem` binary.

See the [plugin setup guide](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.14.0/docs/plugins.md), the [CLI reference](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.14.0/docs/cli.md), and the [MCP reference](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.14.0/docs/mcp.md).

### What's Changed

## Graphmem 0.13.0

This release teaches the code tools a new language and fixes how C and C++ definitions are found. Agentica (`.agc`) files are now outlined and searchable, `find_symbol` can find an import by the last segment of its path, and C/C++ functions that return a pointer or a reference are no longer missing from outlines and searches. The `gmem` binary and the Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi plugin packages are versioned 0.13.0.

### What's new

- **Agentica support.** `code_outline`, `find_symbol`, `code_imports`, and `code_diff` index `.agc` files through [`tree-sitter-agentica`](https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter-agentica) 0.3.0: functions, structs and their fields, enums and their variants, module constants, `type` aliases, and imports, named by path (`std/list`).
- **Imports by last path segment.** With `kind: "import"` (`--kind import`), `find_symbol` ranks an import whose path ends in `/query` with the `.query` suffix matches, in every language: `queue` finds `std/queue`, and `http` finds Go's `net/http`.

### What's fixed

- **C and C++ pointer and reference declarators** ([#41](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/issues/41)). Functions that return a pointer or a reference (`int *f()`, `Box &self()`), including C++ methods, are now outlined and found by name, where before they were silently left out. C globals and struct, union, and class fields are named without their declarators (`global_ptr`, not `*global_ptr`; `buf`, not `buf[16]`), members inside `#if` blocks of a struct or class body are listed, and a C prototype that returns a pointer is no longer listed as a variable.

### Upgrading

For npm installs, upgrade the package and refresh the binary with `gmem-install`:

```sh
npm install --global @sonic182/graphmem@0.13.0
gmem-install
gmem version
```

MCP clients can also run the package directly with `npx -y @sonic182/graphmem@0.13.0 mcp`. For manual installs, download the archive for your platform below and replace the existing `gmem` binary.

The code index format changed, so each checkout's code index is rebuilt automatically the first time a code tool runs after the upgrade. Memories are not affected.

See the [plugin setup guide](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.13.0/docs/plugins.md) and the [CLI reference](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.13.0/docs/cli.md).

## Graphmem 0.12.0

This release makes memory activity and maintenance visible. `gmem health` summarizes access and idle memories, reports logged recalls and inspections, and finds memories whose recorded paths no longer exist. Graphmem also records the source, query, scopes, and ranked results for CLI and MCP searches and inspections, including searches with no results. The `gmem` binary and the Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi plugin packages are versioned 0.12.0.

### What's new

- **Memory health report.** Run `gmem health` to see never-accessed and idle memories by type, recent recall activity, and missing paths cited by memories.
- **Recall activity log.** Searches and inspections now record their source (`cli` or `mcp`), query, scopes, and returned ranked results in the local store.

### What's changed

- **SQLite schema version 2.** The additive migration creates recall event and result tables. Existing stores migrate automatically when opened; their memories and graph data remain intact.

### Upgrading

For npm installs, upgrade the package and refresh the binary with `gmem-install`:

```sh
npm install --global @sonic182/graphmem@0.12.0
gmem-install
gmem version
```

MCP clients can also run the package directly with `npx -y @sonic182/graphmem@0.12.0 mcp`. For manual installs, download the archive for your platform below and replace the existing `gmem` binary.

See the [plugin setup guide](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.12.0/docs/plugins.md), [CLI reference](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.12.0/docs/cli.md), and [schema evolution notes](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.12.0/docs/schema-evolution.md).

## Graphmem 0.11.0

This release makes cross-project memory reads explicit and protects other projects from accidental writes. Discover available scopes through MCP, read another project's memories without changing your write context, and browse the CLI/TUI with the same current-repository defaults as MCP. The `gmem` binary and Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi plugin packages are versioned 0.11.0.

### What's new

- **MCP scope discovery.** The new `list_scopes` tool lists stored scopes, the current scope, and write permissions without changing the read selection or write context.
- **Explicit cross-project CLI reads.** `gmem list` and `gmem show` accept repeatable `--scope` selections. Explicit reads include the selected projects plus `global`, without silently adding the current repository.

### What's changed

- **Consistent read defaults.** CLI and TUI memory reads now default to the current Git repository plus `global`, matching MCP. Outside Git, the default remains `global`.
- **Project-local writes.** Memory creation, updates, and deletion allow only the current repository and `global`. A memory shared with another project remains read-only, even when it is also attached to the current repository or `global`.
- **Transactional flush protection.** `gmem flush --yes` refuses the entire operation without deletion if any memory belongs to a foreign scope.

### What's fixed

- Scoped memory listing applies its limit in SQLite instead of loading the entire selected history before truncating the results.

### Upgrading

**Scope behavior has changed:** if you relied on CLI/TUI reads showing other projects by default, select those scopes explicitly with the CLI. To modify another project's memories, run Graphmem from that repository; MCP clients must restart the server with that repository as its working directory. Selecting a foreign scope for a read does not grant write access. Memories shared across projects remain read-only when any attached scope is foreign.

Use MCP `list_scopes` or CLI `gmem scopes` to discover scope names, then read explicitly:

```sh
gmem list --scope repo:/absolute/path/to/other-project
gmem show 42 --scope repo:/absolute/path/to/other-project
```

To upgrade with explicit binary setup:

```sh
npm install --global @sonic182/graphmem@0.11.0
gmem-install
gmem version
```

Or launch the MCP server with first-run binary setup:

```sh
npx -y @sonic182/graphmem@0.11.0 mcp
```

For Pi:

```sh
pi install npm:@sonic182/graphmem@0.11.0
```

See the [plugin setup guide](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.11.0/docs/plugins.md), [CLI reference](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.11.0/docs/cli.md), and [MCP scope policy](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.11.0/docs/mcp.md).

## Graphmem 0.10.1

This release adds a `graphmem` npm command so MCP clients can launch Graphmem with `npx` and have the native `gmem` binary fetched for them on first run. It also adds the metadata needed to list Graphmem in the official MCP Registry. The `gmem` command is unchanged and still never downloads anything on its own. The `gmem` binary and Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi plugin packages are versioned 0.10.1.

### What's new

- **`graphmem` command.** `npx -y @sonic182/graphmem mcp` now works from a clean machine. On first run it reuses a working `gmem` on your `PATH`, or downloads the matching release binary, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS`, runs a `gmem version` smoke test, and then starts the MCP server. Download progress goes to stderr, so stdout stays reserved for the MCP protocol. Concurrent launches share one download.
- **MCP Registry metadata.** `package.json` now declares `mcpName` (`io.github.sonic182/graphmem`) and the repository ships a `server.json` that passes `mcp-publisher validate`.
- **Release process.** The `new-release` skill now keeps both `server.json` versions in sync, and a test fails if `server.json` drifts from `package.json`.

### What stays the same

- `gmem` and `gmem-install` behave as in 0.10.0: installing the npm package or loading a plugin does not download a binary. Pi still asks before downloading, and OpenCode still reports an explicit installer command.
- Claude Code and Codex plugins still run `gmem` from your `PATH`.

### Also in this release

- Docs: simplified README and plugin setup guides, and a minimal Hugo documentation site deployed with GitHub Pages.
- Evaluation: a Strands agent benchmark for the `gmem` code tools.

### Try it

```sh
npx -y @sonic182/graphmem@0.10.1 mcp
```

To keep the explicit setup instead:

```sh
npm install --global @sonic182/graphmem@0.10.1
gmem-install
gmem version
```

For Pi:

```sh
pi install npm:@sonic182/graphmem@0.10.1
```

See the [plugin setup guide](https://github.com/sonic182/graphmem/blob/0.10.1/docs/plugins.md).
